findings.title: VectorType branch stores bare prefix, nested vectors have no Go type
findings.claim: The VectorType branch still calls NewCustomType with just the prefix instead of the full name, so nested vector types resolve to a bare custom() type with no Go type, causing the PR's own new guard to emit an error and nested vectors can't decode into interface{} at all.

findings.title: Saturation branch of vectorElemMinSize has no test coverage
findings.claim: The overflow-saturation branch in vectorElemMinSize that returns math.MaxInt32 is never exercised by any test; mutation testing shows replacing it with 'return 1' leaves the suite green, unlike every other guard the diff adds.

findings.title: New bound still nil-derefs when SubType is nil and Dimensions > 0
findings.claim: The new guard's comment claims it protects against a nil SubType, but it only covers the Dimensions == 0 case; with Dimensions > 0 and non-nil data, vectorElemMinSize(nil) still panics via nil.Type(), leaving the stated invariant unmet.

findings.title: unmarshalVector bound is based on payload bytes, not real allocation cost
findings.claim: The element-count bound caps against len(data) rather than modeling per-CQL-type allocation cost, leaving up to 56x allocation amplification possible.

findings.title: readBytes slices p[:size] with an unchecked server-supplied length
findings.claim: readBytes performs p[:size] using an attacker/server-controlled size with no bounds check, so a malformed length in any UDT field or tuple element panics on the Scan goroutine with no recover.

findings.title: readTypeInfo slices vector type name assuming trailing ')' and comma
findings.claim: readTypeInfo assumes the custom type spec has a trailing ) and a comma when slicing, so names like ...VectorType, ...VectorType(), or malformed variants cause 'slice bounds out of range' panics on the connection goroutine.

findings.title: Unguarded indexing of split results in type-name parsing
findings.claim: names[1], make([]UDTField, len(names)-2), and spec[1] are indexed without checking the split produced enough parts, causing index-out-of-range or negative-length-slice panics reachable through framer.readTypeInfo; the sibling MapType branch guards the same pattern.

findings.title: unmarshalTuple sets reflect values without an assignability check
findings.claim: unmarshalTuple performs reflect.Set without checking assignability, so e.g. vector<tuple<int,text>,2> into *[][]float32 panics with 'value of type int is not assignable to type float32' instead of returning an unmarshal error.

findings.title: strconv.Atoi error for vector dimension is discarded
findings.claim: The error from parsing the vector dimension via strconv.Atoi is discarded, so a non-numeric dimension silently becomes 0 and an out-of-range one becomes MaxInt64, producing a misleading 'N bytes of data for 0-dimension vector' error instead of surfacing the real parse failure.

findings.title: Unbounded recursion in getCassandraLongType may hang on crafted custom type name
findings.claim: One reviewer reproduced an 80s+ hang with a 98-byte custom name causing thousands of recursive frames in getCassandraLongType, but a follow-up reconciler could not reproduce it on the same commit and downgraded the proposed depth guard to optional, leaving the finding unresolved rather than confirmed.
